newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares higher amid strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares higher amid strong demand.

text.p: Shares traded higher on Monday at the Nigerian stock exchange as the market started another bullish week buoyed by rising demand, traders said.
Most equities appreciated in value, taking the all-share index to 7398.29 from 7364.24 on Friday.
"There was considerable interest in blue chips, especially Cadbury which leapt to a new high as favourable reaction to its full year result posted last week continued," one trader said.
The stock was 28.00 naira, up 91 kobo, as a result.
Nestle and the local bottler of Coca-Cola, Nigerian Bottling Company also ended higher. Nestle went 20 kobo up at 58.50 naira and the bottling firm rose 30 kobo to 39.10 naira.
Banks were in impressive form with First Bank ending 20 kobo up at 11.20 naira while Union Bank and UBA each rose by 10 kobo, closing respectively at 9.85 naira and 8.60 naira.
Dunlop shares gained 15 kobo to 9.45 naira, the same as Industrial Gases which closed at 13.60 naira, both on brighter prospects, said traders.
Oil marketers rose as a result of willing buyers. African Petroleum was 30 kobo up at 52.80 naira, the same as National Oil at 54.70 naira.
Nigerian Breweries closed 15 down because many sellers were dumping large numbers while conglomerate John Holt closed one kobo lower at 9.64 naira.
PZ Industries, which fell steadily last week, closed unchanged although dealers said it was still expected to lose some ground because of profit-taking by investors.
